Registering my support
Changed the channel name: [NEXT] GA - Repeal "Clean Water Act"
Still in support. The target banning fluoridation is insane

Not sure this is necessarily true. The target never defines "contamination", and the dictionary definition that comes up first is 
> the action or state of making or being made impure by polluting or poisoning.
And adding flouride to the water is neither polluting nor poisoning it. 

Had I taken the time to actually read the repeal earlier I would have filed a challenge, actually, as the repeal claims that adding a dye to track pollutants would count as contamination when that's literally the opposite. 

And clause 4 iii of the target makes it clear that chemical additives for health are something nations retain control over, a clause that would be meaningless if the intent was to ban flouridation.

Fluoride is an impurity, as are dyes, and contaminating a water source to track contaminants is still contamination. "Without exception" makes it difficult to argue that some impurities are actually excepted. When I was reviewing the draft, I did notice the section 4 provisions. However, that itself is an issue given that clause 1 says "without exception." It's a wording problem. The repeal specifically makes note of this on my recommendation, though if I was writing it myself I would've probably ditched the "self-regulation" part at the end or connected it better to section 2. Looking at it now, they could've also hit the "may conceivably serve civilians" part that they quote in addition to hitting the "without exception" part, since dumping filtered waste into a body of water that doesn't serve civilians is still banned if it could "conceivably" serve them in the future. Imagine the consequences for sewage systems

That said, while those 2 changes would be nice to have in hindsight, I think the current repeal makes a more than adequate case. It's not a situation where a repeal solely complains about pointy desk corners in a target that bans having a government
@Archon FOR btw
Sorry for the delay. I though this goes to vote tomorrow for some reason
Smh
Fired
Changed the channel name: [AT VOTE - FOR] GA - Repeal "Clean Water Act"
Deliberate additives are not impurities.
For something to be a chemical impurity it would have to be unwanted or result in an unintended composition.
Since the addition of Flouride is necessary to produce flouridated tapwater, it's not an impurity.
By that logic, raw sewage isn’t an impurity because it’s necessary to produce ~~raw sewage water~~ State+ Enhanced Tap™️
The target should’ve listed exceptions instead of saying “no exceptions!” and then doing a weird reserved areas thing at the bottom
“It isn’t contamination if it’s intentional” is a bad argument
Especially when the target explicitly calls it intentional contamination
Strictly, it does ban fluoridation. I agree with Cretox.
It's one of those "If *I* was writing this it would be better, but this is still fine" repeals
There's somewhat of a contradiction between clauses one and four.
Of the original resolution, that is.
Clause 1 actively undermines 4 and clause 1's "no exceptions!" undermines arguments like EP's
Exactly. 👍
I can see what they were going for but they just executed poorly
I haven't read your back-and-forth, but my reading of the original resolution is that its wording is too strong and inflexible for its own good.
i don’t agree with adding anything but i do agree with the repeal due to how unclear the original resolution is with its definitions, so i am in favor
Say, Julez, you have a WA nation in the region, correct?
yes
i try to vote on every resolution
If you tell me the nation's name I can get you masked as "Residents [WA]" and Hussar of the East, possibly.
i think i am on the TEP forums but i’m not sure i don’t go on much
my nation is Leore
Well, yeah. Are you arguing that the target literally prevents nations from having sewer systems?
Because sewer systems would be potential water sources, but the presence of waste in them is intentional.
The way you're interpreting it (that literally anything other than H2O counts as contamination and there's no exceptions) would make the target impossible to comply with.

I'm saying that by your logic of "deliberate additives are not impurities" and "for something to be a chemical impurity it would have to be unwanted or result in an unintended composition," raw sewage also isn't an impurity if deliberately added to a water source. Which would be silly. It's a bad argument
The target is poorly written, yes
Resolutions don't have to be reasonable just because they passed

If you are deliberately adding raw sewage to a water source because you want the raw sewage to be there and that is the desired outcome, then yes, that's not a contaminant. How is that a bad argument?

No, but presumably the interpretation has to result in it being possible to comply with the resolution. Otherwise, if noncompliance is the only option, the target doesn't actually do anything since nations cannot comply.
Ok so factories dumping their waste into the water is ok because they want it to be there
The government doesn't want it there.
WA resolutions act on member nations, not random factories.

The only alternative to this is to argue that the target bans the use of any sewage system since they all, by necessity, add sewage to water. That's such an absurd interpretation that it wouldn't make any sense. Obviously the deliberate addition of sewage to a water source (as part of a sewage system) is intended and therefore not contamination.
TEP votes FOR. Resolution passes. (5-3-0-0)
Changed the channel name: [Passed] GA - Repeal "Clean Water Act"
